title: No Kings movement holds early voting mobilization events in Washington
seoTitle: Washington No Kings early voting rally

tea.why: Protesters gathered to encourage early voting, build volunteer networks, and push back against potential election sabotage before the midterms.
tea.want: Organizers want a large early voter turnout to ease burdens on election workers, avoid long lines, and secure midterm election results.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Demonstrators gathered at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., to dance, listen to music, and urge voters to cast ballots early.

summary: The No Kings coalition, alongside groups like Indivisible and 50501, organized nationwide events on Saturday, October 17, 2026, to encourage early voting ahead of the US midterm elections. In Washington, D.C., demonstrators gathered at the Lincoln Memorial holding signs with messages such as 'VOTE EARLY' and 'HANDS OFF MY VOTE!' while a band entertained the crowd. According to organizers, the strategy aims to build a volunteer network ready to defend election results, prevent voter intimidation, and increase voter turnout to protect against potential sabotage. The movement initially formed in response to policies during Donald Trump's second presidential term.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

crowd.text: what appeared to be a few hundred people

updates.text: Demonstrators gathered at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., for a No Kings early voting rally.
